## LTT v0.1.2

The first public build of a Windows dictionary that answers offline in milliseconds. Double-tap the hotkey and the word under the cursor is looked up; drag a box over a screen region and Windows' own OCR reads it instead. Everything is answered from a local SQLite dictionary — no network request, no account, and nothing to log in to.

## New

### Lookup that degrades instead of failing

Five tiers, each one only filling the results the previous tiers left missing:

1. an exact match on the main dictionary (`normalized_word` index);
2. a user-dictionary entry, matched exactly, or by a substring of its translation or example;
3. tokenised candidates matched exactly one by one — Latin text split on spaces and punctuation, Chinese with a 2–4 character sliding window;
4. an FTS5 prefix search over the full text, ordered by `rank`;
5. an edit-distance fallback (OSA distance, with a budget of 1 up to four characters, 2 up to eight, 3 above that) — which is what turns `helo` into `halo` and `wrold` into `world`.

- A word you saved yourself always wins over the main dictionary's entry for the same word, and the tiers stop filling a field as soon as it has a result, so a good exact hit is not diluted by fuzzy ones.
- Results open in their own always-on-top window, kept out of the taskbar, so a hotkey lookup never overwrites the query window you already had open.

### Reading the screen

- **Selection** — the hotkey path is clipboard-safe: `Ctrl+C` is sent, the selection is read, and the previous clipboard content is restored afterwards, so a lookup does not cost you what you had copied.
- **Region capture** — a translucent full-screen overlay to drag a box over, then `Windows.Media.Ocr` reads it, preferring the OCR languages you have installed.
- Both hotkeys — modifiers plus virtual-key code — are stored in `settings.json`; a corrupt file falls back to the defaults instead of blocking startup.

### Tray and user dictionary

- Closing the query window hides it to the tray; the tray menu carries 打开, 划词翻译, 截图翻译, 设置 and 退出, each translation action showing its hotkey.
- Your own entries live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TranslateLite\user_dictionary.db`, next to but separate from the main dictionary, so replacing or upgrading the dictionary never overwrites them.
- The manager window adds, edits (double-click a row), deletes, filters by word, translation or tag, and bulk-imports a tab-separated file — one entry per line, `#` comments ignored:

```text
word<TAB>translation[<TAB>definition[<TAB>example]]
```

### Dictionary data and build

- The main dictionary is built from ECDICT and CC-CEDICT, imported into SQLite with FTS5; the import path is described in the README rather than shipped as a binary.
- `dotnet publish` or the publish script produce a self-contained Windows build; the executable and its taskbar icon are now the project's own — a white rounded tile with an open book and two speech bubbles, transparent outside the tile, as a multi-size `.ico`.
- Stack: .NET 8 · WPF · SQLite FTS5 · `Windows.Media.Ocr`.

## Fixes

- `userCommand` is now disposed with `await using`, so a user-dictionary command cannot outlive the lookup that created it.
- The C# sources were normalised (escaped characters restored, style unified) so the project builds without warnings from the style pass.

## Notes

- Windows only, and the OCR path needs an OCR language pack installed in Windows itself; the dictionary, user dictionary and settings all live under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TranslateLite`.
